chunks: The aversion to plenitude (or the desire for increase) occupied you.

key_terms.التَّكَاثُرُ: The desire for increase or accumulation (of wealth, children, status), leading to distraction.

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'Al-Takathur' in Surah Al-Takathur?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a critique of the 'accumulation mindset' (takathur) that characterizes pre-Islamic and contemporary materialism, where the race for worldly dominance blinds individuals to the inevitability of death and divine accountability. Scholars highlight that this distraction prevents the cultivation of taqwa (God-consciousness), urging believers to redirect their competitive energy toward acquiring spiritual merits and good deeds that will accompany them beyond the grave.
